A solid circular shaft of uniform diameter d = 30 mm and length L = 1200 mm is modeled as a linear-elastic, small-deformation torsion member.
The material is AISI 1020 steel with shear modulus G = 76923.1 MPa.
All quantities are expressed in the N–mm–MPa unit system.
The shaft is fixed (clamped) at x = 0, providing a reaction torque, and is free at x = L = 1200 mm with no rotational constraint.
Two external torques are applied: T1 = +200000 N·mm at the free tip (x = 1200 mm) and T2 = −200000 N·mm at x = 400 mm, using a right-hand-rule sign convention where positive torque vector points in the +x direction.
The polar moment of inertia is J = π d⁴ / 32 = π (30)⁴ / 32 ≈ 79521.6 mm⁴ and is constant over the full length.
The governing relation is the torsion differential equation dθ/dx = T(x) / (G J), where T(x) is the internal torque at position x.
The internal torque distribution is T(x) = 0 for 0 ≤ x < 400 mm and T(x) = +200000 N·mm for 400 < x ≤ 1200 mm, obtained by sectioning the shaft and summing external torques on the free (right) side of each cut.
The reaction torque at the fixed end x = 0 is zero, since T1 + T2 = 0 and global moment equilibrium requires R = −(T1 + T2) = 0.
The shear stress at radius ρ in the cross-section at position x is τ(ρ, x) = T(x) ρ / J.
The maximum shear stress occurs at the outer surface (ρ = d/2 = 15 mm) in the loaded segment and equals τ_max = T_max (d/2) / J = 200000 × 15 / 79521.6 ≈ 37.73 MPa.
The angle of twist as a function of position is θ(x) = (1/(G J)) ∫₀ˣ T(ξ) dξ, giving θ(x) = 0 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 400 mm and θ(x) = 200000 (x − 400) / (G J) for 400 ≤ x ≤ 1200 mm.
The total angle of twist at the free end is θ(L) = 200000 × 800 / (76923.1 × 79521.6) ≈ 0.02616 rad (approximately 1.498 degrees).
The additional assumption is that the shaft is prismatic (constant cross-section), the loading is purely torsional with no axial force, bending moment, or transverse shear, and the material behaves elastically throughout (no yielding, no plasticity).
